remparts_page.name: Ramparts & Bastion of the Angel
remparts_page.hero_subtitle: Walk the Portuguese sea walls for Atlantic views and the iconic Bastion of the Angel.
remparts_page.overview.title: Stone against the Atlantic
remparts_page.overview.p1: The ramparts of the Portuguese City still draw a hard line between the medina and the ocean. The Bastion of the Angel is the standout viewpoint — a sea-facing platform that appears in almost every El Jadida photo essay.
remparts_page.overview.p2: Walk the accessible sections for wind, horizon and a sense of how Mazagan was fortified. Surfaces can be uneven; wear steady shoes and mind the drop toward the rocks.
remparts_page.overview.p3: Sunset is popular. Pair the walls with the cistern earlier the same day for a complete Portuguese circuit.

remparts_page.faq.title: Ramparts & Bastion of the Angel FAQ
remparts_page.faq.q1.question: Is access free?
remparts_page.faq.q1.answer: Wall walks are generally free; some platforms may have local rules — follow posted signs.
remparts_page.faq.q2.question: Wind on the bastion?
remparts_page.faq.q2.answer: Often strong. Bring a layer even in summer.
remparts_page.faq.q3.question: Good for children?
remparts_page.faq.q3.answer: With close supervision near edges; not ideal for toddlers.
remparts_page.faq.q4.question: How long?
remparts_page.faq.q4.answer: One to two hours for a full wall circuit with photo stops.
remparts_page.faq.q5.question: Best light?
remparts_page.faq.q5.answer: Late afternoon and sunset for warm colour on the stone.
